title: Andy Ogles thanks colleagues for support on parental rights and calls for changes to H-1B program
text:
← Back to the wire
Andy Ogles thanks colleagues for support on parental rights and calls for changes to H-1B program
On October 8, 2026, Rep. Andy Ogles highlighted his efforts on parental rights and called for significant reforms to U.S. immigration policies via several tweets.
Rep. Andy Ogles, U.S. Congressman representing Tennessee's 5th district, posted several messages on his Twitter account on October 8, 2026, focusing on parental rights and immigration policy.
In one tweet from October 8, 2026, Ogles expressed appreciation for fellow legislators and an advocacy group by stating, "Thank you to @RepJimBaird, @RepSherriBiggs, @Rep_Davidson, @RepClayFuller, @RepMcCormick, @RepMaryMiller, @RepJohnRose, and @approject for joining the fight for parental rights."
Shortly after this post, Ogles shared a link with the message, "Read More Here: https://t.co/mkgRCSu22L" (October 8, 2026).
Later in the day on October 8, 2026, Ogles addressed issues surrounding the H-1B visa program and U.S. immigration policy. He wrote, "YES! The H-1B scam has ripped off American workers and destroyed our culture. @VP is doing what most never had the guts to do: call it out and end the fraud. My ASSIMILATION Act will support this move by gutting the H-1B program and repealing the Hart-Celler Act, which has https://t.co/CxbD4pvtTP"
The H-1B visa program allows U.S. employers to temporarily employ foreign workers in specialty occupations; it has been a topic of debate due to concerns about its impact on American workers and wages. The Hart-Celler Act of 1965 ended earlier national origins quotas in U.S. immigration law and significantly changed the demographic composition of immigrants entering the United States.
Ogles’ posts reflect ongoing legislative discussions around parental rights as well as debates over employment-based immigration programs in Congress.
